run_summary.gft_basis_note: Dense binary Hamming graphlets use the Walsh basis as the graph Fourier basis; Laplacian eigenvalue is 2 * Walsh order.

scientific_conclusion: RUN-065 shows that a sparse residual field can create held-out local topology in the sampled reference/consensus-like graphlets while maintaining a low-order-dominated Walsh/GFT spectrum. It does not validate broad procedural generalization across starting regions, and it does not show that DCA/contact placement adds biological structure beyond strength- and density-matched controls.
